query: On that day, I attended a smaller music festival after a friend invited me, and the spontaneity of the invitation made it feel even more exciting. It was such a wonderful surprise to find myself at an event that felt intimate and personal, unlike the overwhelming crowds I often encountered at larger festivals. As I walked through the festival grounds, I could feel the energy of the music flowing around me, creating an inviting atmosphere that was both chill and engaging. The artists performing were incredibly talented, each bringing their unique style to the stage, which kept me on my toes and captivated. It was a refreshing experience to connect with not only the music but also the people around me, sharing smiles and nodding along to the tunes, something I hardly ever felt at the massive events I usually attended.

query: I also took a big step forward and started taking piano lessons! I’ve found so much joy in my earlier ukulele classes that I wanted to explore composition beyond just the ukulele. The ukulele brought me a flavor of music that I never knew could exist in my life, and I felt a spark of creativity igniting within me. As I plucked those strings and strummed simple chords, it was as if I was not only learning an instrument but also unlocking a door to a world of musical expression that I desperately wanted to delve deeper into. The challenge of learning the piano, with its rich history and intricate melodies, excites me because I believe it will significantly enhance my ability to compose and experiment with different styles and genres of music.
